question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (SIA) notes that skill-training graduates who were employed at month 6 show only 70% retention at month 24. In SROI terminology, this fade-over-time is captured as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Drop-off is the reduction of outcome over time after the intervention ends. If 100% are employed at month 6 and 70% remain employed at month 24, drop-off is 30% over that horizon. It is applied year-by-year to the projected outcome stream in multi-year SROI. The Trap: Deadweight = what would have happened anyway. Displacement = outcome produced at another group's expense. Attribution = credit to partners. Only drop-off captures temporal fade. Cross-Exam Context: XXIII Ch 5 introduces outcome sustainability; IMP dimension HOW MUCH includes 'duration' which overlaps with drop-off economics. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When reading an SE's SROI narrative, check the drop-off rate year-by-year — many SEs apply a flat 10% when the reality is front-loaded (large drop in year 2, smaller thereafter). Model both and disclose sensitivity.
